articles.title: St Johnstone 2-1 Hibs: Josh Fowler scores twice as St Johnstone leapfrog opponents in table
articles.summary: Report as Josh Fowler scored two goals for St Johnstone in a 2-1 victory against Hibernian; Nathan Lowe was on target for the visitors
articles.body:
Fowler netted from close range on 16 minutes then slotted home a penalty after Nathan Lowe had levelled for Hibs to secure Saints' second win of the campaign.

The visitors were the better team in the second period but Simo Valakari's team held on for a 2-1 success to move into seventh spot.

Fowler, who scored a late equaliser off the bench in midweek at Dundee, fully justified his return to the starting line-up.

The striker scored with the first chance of the contest. Hibs backed off Jason Holt, permitting the Perth captain to reach the 18-yard box and play in Taylor Steven, whose low cross took a nick off the heel of Adam Mayor and landed with Fowler at the back post.

The striker did well to adjust to the deflection and tuck a right-footed finish past Raphael Sallinger.

That good work was undone on 29 minutes by a slack Reece McAlear pass in the centre of the park. Miguel Chaiwa sent Lowe sprinting clear and the on-loan Stoke forward placed a low shot between Toby Steward and his right-hand post.

Saints did well to shrug that mishap off and deservedly retook the lead four minutes from half-time.

Bosnian full-back Enes Alic drove into the penalty box and was nudged over by Martin Boyle. Fowler buried his fourth Premiership goal of the campaign to the bottom right, sending Sallinger the wrong way.

Fowler twice came close to a hat-trick early in the second period, before his 72nd-minute withdrawal.

But it was Hibs who looked most likely to score for large parts of the half.

Kanayo Megwa, who replaced injured Grant Hanley on the hour, met a corner with a powerful back-post header but Steward conjured a brilliant one-handed stop on his line.

Saints brought on Matty Todd and reverted to a back five to see off the threat, although there were some frantic moments of defending.

The hosts were grateful when sub Thibault Klidje struck a good chance off his own man Ante Suto.

Alic forced Sallinger into a fine save as Saints menaced on the break but Valakari's men did enough to see out victory and condemn Hibs to back-to-back defeats.

"It was a good win and an important win. I think there was everything across the 90 minutes.

"In the first half we played some excellent football, progressing our passes and were very solid.

"In the second half we had to show the other side of our game - this grittiness and readiness to put our bodies on the line and block shots. And Toby (Steward) had to make a couple of big saves.

"Josh is showing that he can score goals at this level. I have never doubted that - and Josh himself never doubted that. Of course, strikers live for goals and when you score them you get so much confidence."

"The biggest thing for me is the manner in which the first half went for us - again.

"It was summed up in the way we conceded the two goals. So, a lack of desire to stop somebody advancing past you, gambling in the box, guessing in the box.

"Then a needless penalty that we give away. They were poor goals. But the players went to the end and we created a few chances.

"But I certainly can't sit here and say we deserved to win the game. Back-to-back defeats is tough to take. And, understandably so, criticism will be there."

articles.title: Hearts 2-1 Dundee: Sabah Kerjota's stoppage-time strike snatches victory to make it four wins on the spin
articles.summary: Report as Hearts leave it late to complete comeback and beat Dundee to make it four league wins on the bounce
articles.body:
Hearts were frustrated for long periods after the visitors - who had both Joe Westley and Fin Robertson stretchered off - took the lead in the 17th minute through Bradley Fink.

But Hearts eventually drew level in the 84th minute through a Claudio Braga penalty before Dundee had Zan Besir sent off as the match ticked into stoppage time.

Wouter Vrancken's buoyant side made their extra man count when Albanian substitute Kerjota drilled in his first goal since arriving at Tynecastle last summer in the sixth minute of added time.

The victory elevated the Jambos, unbeaten in eight in all competitions, to second in the table.

There was one enforced tweak to the Hearts side that started Thursday's Edinburgh derby triumph away to Hibernian as Blair Spittal, who is facing months on the sidelines due to injury, was replaced by Tomas Magnusson.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley made four changes from Wednesday's 1-1 draw with St Johnstone as Imari Samuels, Drey Wright, Robertson and Fink were all added.

Hearts started brightly and Calvin Miller saw an effort deflected behind in the third minute. From the resulting corner, Dundee suffered a blow as Westley had to leave the field on a stretcher after a collision with Jamie McCart. Bobby Wales came on in his place.

The visitors made the breakthrough from their first chance of the match in the 17th minute when Fink got in behind Oisin McEntee to latch on to Samuels' long ball over the top and the Swiss forward looped an effort beyond the exposed Beau Reus from 12 yards.

Dundee threatened a second when Ethan Hamilton seized on an error from Magnusson and surged forward but his low shot from just outside the box ran wide of Reus' left-hand post.

Hearts, having been knocked out of their rhythm by the visitors in the first half, had a good opportunity five minutes after the break when Josh McPake ran on to Magnusson's pass and drove into the box but he was denied by Owen Goodman.

At the other end, Dundee substitute Jack Moorhouse's shot skimmed the crossbar after he dispossessed Jordi Altena.

Hearts started to crank up the pressure as the half wore on, with James Wilson, Braga, sub JJ Williams and McPake all threatening.

Dundee then had a second player stretchered off in the 76th minute when Robertson went down injured.

Hearts eventually levelled in the 84th minute when they were awarded a penalty following a VAR intervention after Owen Bevan was adjudged to have blocked a Christian Borchgrevink cutback with his arm, and Braga stepped up to send Goodman the wrong way.

Dundee suffered further woe in the 90th minute when sub Besir was shown a red card for a reckless challenge on Magnusson, and they were punished again as Kerjota rifled home a low angled finish after a short corner was worked to him just inside the box.

"If you win a derby and you then lose this weekend, you bring the focus on the negative; you lose the emotion of the derby a bit.

"So after a setback in a difficult game and against a side who defended really low, I was really happy to see that we stayed in the game and we kept pushing to get what we deserved, and at the end they did it.

"It's also good to see that the players don't panic and that they have the resilience and quality to turn those situations around because you have to have it when you want to try to fight for the top spots in the league."

"It was a challenging afternoon, yet we nearly got a really positive outcome," he said. "It was a really difficult game to manage in the respect that we had so many enforced changes.

"There were so many things to deal with. When I consider all the challenges that I had, and the players were faced with on the pitch, I thought they were incredible in their attitude and performance.

"Not in terms of controlling the game or having periods of possession, but just the will and desire and determination to try and get a result."

articles.standfirst: El alemán, feliz con su equipo aunque apunta que siempre se puede mejorar
articles.summary: El alemán, feliz con su equipo aunque apunta que siempre se puede mejorar
articles.body: Hansi Flick analizó el partido frente al Valencia. El técnico estaba feliz después de claro triunfo que consiguió su equipo. Eso sí, quiere que su equipo controle más los partidos aunque le gustó mucho lo que vio de sus ugadores en Mestalla. "Ha sido fantástico hemos dominado el partido desde el principio. Hemos controlado y dominado. Es lo que quiero ver." "Para mí lo importante son los tres puntos, pero tenemos calidad en el campo. Podemos atacar bien contra bloques bajos y espacialmente con esta temperatura." "No ha cambiado nada. Tenemos mucha calidad en ataque, también en el centro del campo. Estoy feliz que Pedri haya ganado. Tenemos la calidad para generar ocasiones y eso es bueno". "Tenemos muchos jugadores de gran calidad y eso tengo que manejarlo. No es fácil. En el fútbol las cosas cambian muy rápido. Estoy muy contento con los minutos de Olmo que siempre quiere más. Y que lo haga entrando desde el banquillo y tomando las mejores decisiones para el equipo" "Tiene mucha intensidad dentro y fuera del área. Recupera balones. Tiene mucha intensidad con la pelota. A veces se equivoca, pero lo está haciendo muy bien". "Estamos felices de que esté en nuestro equipo. De lo que hace con la pelota y por el equipo. Pero también quiero destacar el buen trabajo de Marc Bernal. Él va mejorando. Rodri es increíble no solo en el campo, también en el vestuario. Es un líder. "La primea de Cubarsí la tenía que hacer. Es así y tenemos que aceptarlo, el árbitro ha hecho gran partido". "Después de un 0-5 seguimos atacando, atacando y atacando, quiero controlar más los partidos. Y hay que ahorrar energía. Siempre podemos mejorar, nunca nada es perfecto". "Ayer entrenó y no tenía problemas. Esta mañana hemos hablado y me ha dicho que podía jugar, que estaba bien".

articles.title: "Siempre os llevaré conmigo, vuestro "Pelusa": Así se despide Carlos Álvarez
articles.standfirst: El actual jugador del Club América ha querido dedicar unas palabras a todo el levantinismo
articles.summary: El actual jugador del Club América ha querido dedicar unas palabras a todo el levantinismo
articles.body: Hay despedidas que duelen. Y para los aficionados del Levante, la venta de Carlos Álvarez al Club América, aún más. Después de que su club hiciera oficial su incorporación, el jugador andaluz ha querido dedicar unas palabras, a través de sus redes sociales, agradeciendo y mostrando su amor al club y a la afición granota. El atacante ha valorado la labor del club valenciano por la oportunidad de jugar en el fútbol profesional "aun chaval de 20 años" y la dificultar de salir de casa por primera vez. Así mismo, ha manifestado que llegaba con el objetivo de mejorar y cumplir sueños, aunque no imaginaba lo que vendría posteriormente. "Llegaba con ganas de mejorar, con motivación, con trabajo, pero sobre todo con la ilusión del que estaba acercándose a los sueños que había imaginado de pequeño. Lo que nunca soñé es todo lo que viviría después, un club y una afición que me hacía sentirme como en casa, unos compañeros magníficos, que sin duda me llevaré para toda la vida y como no, el ascenso", apunta el jugador. Después de tres años en la entidad del barrio de Orriols, al jugador le resulta complicado elegir un recuerdo, aunque sin lugar a dudas, pone en valor el ascenso a Primera División en Burgos, donde lo cita como " nuestra revancha". "Son tantos los recuerdos bonitos que tengo que es muy difícil elegir uno, pero si tuviese que hacerlo, sin duda, ese 25 de mayo saboreamos la gloria. El partido, el momento, el palo de años atrás y ese minuto 96, ese mágico minuto que hizo que lo vivido en un pasado se terminase de cerrar. Fue nuestra revancha y lo conseguimos entre todos, desde el primer jugador al último aficionado", escribe Carlos Álvarez. El andaluz concluye el comunicado con la "conciencia tranquila", después de todo el esfuerzo realizado y el inicio de una nueva etapa en su vida, con otros sueños por conseguir y seguir creciendo como futbolista. Con la camiseta azulgrana, Carlos Álvarez ha disputado un total de 105 partidos oficiales, entre competición liguera y Copa del Rey, y donde consiguió anotar catorce goles.

articles.title: 20-year wait ends: India qualify for AFC U20 Asian Cup with 3-0 win over Bangladesh
articles.summary: Football News: India booked their place in the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament for the first time in 20 years after beating Bangladesh 3-0 in their final qualifyin.
articles.body: India booked their place in the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament for the first time in 20 years after beating Bangladesh 3-0 in their final qualifying match on Sunday.The victory was India's second in three matches and took them to six points. However, they had to wait for the result of the later Syria vs Uzbekistan match to confirm their qualification.With Syria losing 0-3 to Uzbekistan, India finished second in Group B and qualified for the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament after 20 years as one of the seven best runners-up teams across the eight groups. India last played in the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament in 2006.Uzbekistan also qualified as group toppers with nine points. Syria finished third with three points, and bottom-placed Bangladesh were relegated to the Development Phase after losing all three games. The main tournament will be held in China from March 24 to April 10, 2027.Danny Meitei Laishram opened the scoring in the 25th minute before Vishal Yadav doubled India's advantage with an acrobatic finish on the hour mark. Substitute Md Arbash then sealed the contest with a powerful strike in the 79th minute.The match began on an even keel, with neither side able to establish control during the opening exchanges.India took the lead in the 25th minute through an excellent piece of coordinated pressing and attacking play. Danny put Md Abdul Riyad Fahim under pressure and forced the Bangladesh defender into conceding possession cheaply to Hateem Ali.The Indian striker displayed excellent awareness as he took on two defenders before laying the ball off for the unmarked Danny inside the penalty area. Danny kept his composure and applied the finish to put India ahead in the crucial contest.The goal lifted the Blue Colts, who began dictating the tempo, retaining possession and patiently probing for a second. Danny nearly doubled the advantage in the 34th minute when his looping free-kick dipped dangerously towards goal, but Bangladesh goalkeeper Raj Chowdhury remained alert and made the save.India resumed after the interval in the same manner in which they had ended the first half, keeping Bangladesh under pressure and searching for another goal.The second goal arrived in the 60th minute. A long throw into the penalty area was flicked on by Rishikanta towards Vishal, who produced an acrobatic finish to beat Chowdhury and stun the Bangladesh defence.Bangladesh attempted to mount a comeback after falling two goals behind and began playing with greater aggression. India remained organised at the back, though, absorbing the pressure without allowing their opponents a way back into the match.India head coach Mahesh Gawali introduced Md Arbash and Prashan Jajo in the 72nd minute, replacing Danny and Vishal. The change soon paid off as Arbash put the result beyond doubt seven minutes later.Yaipharemba Chingakham initiated the move before India exchanged a series of passes to unlock the Bangladesh defence. Arbash completed the attack with a powerful left-footed strike into the roof of the net, making it 3-0.Gawali made three further changes during the closing stages, introducing Aniket Yadav, Omang Dodum and Daniyal Makakmayum as India comfortably saw out the remainder of the match.(With inputs from PTI)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lamine Yamal and Fermin Lopez star as Barcelona run riot at Valencia
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal scored twice and Fermin Lopez shone as Barcelona romped to a 5-0 win at La Liga strugglers Valencia.
articles.body:
Fermin Lopez scored a goal and created two others as champions Barcelona eased to a 5-0 victory over hosts Valencia in their La Liga clash on Sunday to maintain their perfect start to the new football season.

Lamine Yamal (two), Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for the visitors, who controlled the contest from the start and lead the LaLiga table with 12 points from four games, three more than second-placed Real Madrid.

Valencia are rooted to the bottom of the table with a single point from their four games and never looked like getting anything from this encounter.

Barca took the lead inside six minutes when Fermin’s pass into the box was latched onto by Yamal, who lifted his shot over home goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski from a tight angle.

Fermin then drilled in a second from 18 yards on 22 minutes after being teed up by Anthony Gordon, before he turned provider again.

He got in behind the Valencia defence from a Yamal pass, and his ball across the six-yard box was tapped in by Raphinha at the back post on 50 minutes.

Those two proved a potent combination, and twice more, Fermin fed Raphinha for excellent chances. But the latter saw his first effort saved and could not get a good connection on the second.

Rodri struck the crossbar with a header as Barca created chances at will, and it was no surprise when Pedri slotted in a fourth on 79 minutes.

Barca handed a debut to Gabriel Jesus off the bench following his move from Arsenal, and there was time for one more goal as Yamal swept home his second from close range as the visitors took their tally of goals in La Liga this season to 17 in four games.

articles.title: ‘Cheating and still losing!’: Ronaldo slammed after being caught spying on rival’s tactics in season’s first defeat
articles.summary: Football News: Cristiano Ronaldo's cheeky attempt to spy on Al-Ittihad's tactics sparks controversy as Al-Nassr suffers their first loss of the season; social media reaction ensues.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has never been one to leave a competitive edge unexplored.But even by Ronaldo's standards, his latest attempt to gain an advantage was rather cheeky.The Al-Nassr captain was caught on camera appearing to sneak a look at Al-Ittihad defender Danilo's tactical instructions during Saturday's Saudi Pro League clash, producing one of the lighter moments in an otherwise fiercely contested night.Unfortunately for Ronaldo, the laughs did not last quite as long as the joke.Ronaldo caught peeking at Al-Ittihad's tacticsThe amusing incident unfolded during a tense spell when Danilo received a slip of paper containing tactical instructions from the Al-Ittihad bench.Ronaldo immediately positioned himself alongside the defender and appeared to take the opportunity to have a quick look at what was written on the note.Danilo soon noticed what his opponent was doing, turning towards Ronaldo as the two shared a smile.For a moment, the light-hearted exchange cut through the tension of a fiercely contested match.But Ronaldo's attempt at tactical espionage ultimately did little to help Al-Nassr.The Portuguese forward played the full 90 minutes, but could not find the goal that would have rescued his side from their first defeat of the season.His best effort was denied by Predrag Rajkovic, with the Al-Ittihad goalkeeper producing an outstanding second-half display to protect his team's advantage.And after the final whistle, Al-Ittihad appeared to have the last laugh.The Jeddah club posted a message on X aimed directly at their opponents, captioning it:“Cheating and still losing!”The post appeared to refer to Ronaldo's attempt to look at the written tactical instructions, adding an extra sting to what had already been a frustrating evening for the Al-Nassr captain.Ilenikhena double ends Al-Nassr's perfect startThe result was a significant setback for Ange Postecoglou, whose honeymoon period at Al-Nassr came crashing down against an impressive Al-Ittihad side.Al-Ittihad needed only four minutes to take the lead.George Ilenikhena rose to head home from close range, immediately putting Al-Nassr under pressure.The striker thought he had doubled the advantage shortly afterwards when he raced through and found the net, only for the effort to be ruled out for offside.He did not have to wait long for another opportunity.In the 22nd minute, Ilenikhena collected a pass from Houssem Aouar before lifting a superb finish over the goalkeeper to make it 2-0.Al-Nassr responded before half-time.João Félix saw his effort saved by Rajkovic, but Angelo Gabriel reacted quickest to the rebound and reduced the deficit before the break.That proved to be Al-Nassr's only breakthrough.Rajkovic stood firm throughout the second half, denying Ronaldo and his teammates as Ittihad held on for a statement victory.The defeat leaves Al-Nassr three points behind league leaders Al-Hilal, while Al-Ittihad climbed to fourth place with 11 points.There was also controversy surrounding Al-Nassr's goal, with Al-Ittihad supporters arguing that Angelo's effort should have been ruled out for offside.None of it changed the outcome.Al-Ittihad had the three points, Al-Nassr had their first defeat of the season and Ronaldo had been unable to turn his cheeky attempt to uncover the opposition's tactics into anything tangible.At least he got a laugh out of Danilo.Al-Ittihad, however, made sure they got the final word.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Corberán: “La situación nos deja tocados, pero no hundidos”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Valencia asegura que se ve con fuerzas para enderezar el rumbo del equipo
articles.summary: El técnico del Valencia asegura que se ve con fuerzas para enderezar el rumbo del equipo
articles.body: Carlos Corberán compareció ante los medios tras la durísima derrota del Valencia ante el Barcelona (0-5) en una noche marcada por algo más que el resultado. Mientras Mestalla descargaba una protesta masiva contra la propiedad, la directiva, el entrenador y los jugadores, el técnico valencianista tuvo que dar explicaciones después de una goleada que agrava la crisis deportiva del equipo y aumenta la fractura entre la afición y el club. Si lo de Riazor dijo que fue una vergüenza, ¿hoy cómo lo califica?: “"Hoy analizo el partido contra un rival que ha sido superior a nosotros de principio a fin. Encajar un gol tan pronto lo ponía todo cuesta arriba. Las ocasiones que tuvimos tras ese gol, en transiciones rápidas, no las aprovechamos y hubiera sido importante. Y el rival encontró la fórmula para hundirnos. Después del tercer gol fue difícil darle la vuelta”. ¿El entrenador del Valencia tiene fuerza para levantar esta situación? “Es una situación que nos deja todos tocados, pero tampoco nos deja hundidos. Es una situación difícil, pero vamos a buscar soluciones como equipo, con honestidad y trabajo. Es un momento en el que aceptamos cualquier crítica a nosotros, porque la afición empieza la temporada con una ilusión grande y como entrenador no he conseguido que podamos darle esa ilusión o ese nivel. Nos toca transitar ese momento a nosotros juntos para encontrar las soluciones y cambiar la dinámica. ¿Pero usted tiene ánimo y fuerza? ¿se plantea dimitir? “Yo siempre tengo fuerza y convicción desde que cogí este trabajo: Tengo la responsabilidad de darle la vuelta a una situación que ha empezado más complicada que el año pasado. Pero con convicción y trabajo tenemos que darle la vuelta”. ¿Y cuál es la solución para este Valencia? “Hoy no he visto falta de actitud. Lo que he visto es que lo que ha propuesto el Barcelona ha superado lo que nosotros hemos propuesto. Al final aquí todos los somos los responsables de lo que vivimos y los que podemos cambiar la dinámica del Valencia. Desde ese compromiso afrontamos el momento”. ¿Qué capacidad de reacción tiene el equipo y si tuviera que explicarle al presidente Kiat Lim lo que está pasando, qué le diría? “Las conversaciones con Kiat siempre han sido honestas, sinceras, haciéndole sentir las necesidades o preocupaciones. Es momento de encontrar esas soluciones, de vivir este momento como equipo, es un momento difícil para los jugadores, porque acumular resultados negativos hace que puedas rendir por debajo de tus posibilidades. Estamos viviendo por debajo de lo que somos capaces de hacer. He visto al equipo rendir mejor”.

articles.title: Everton 2-2 Manchester United: Red Devils frustrated but Michael Carrick still optimistic
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick remains optimistic despite his side dropping another two points at Everton.
articles.body:
There are positives for Manchester United to take from their 2-2 draw at Everton .

Striker Benjamin Sesko scored his first goal of a season - the start to which has been delayed for longer than anticipated by a shin injury.

Kobbie Mainoo has impressed in the campaign as a whole so far and shows no sign of being affected by his unhappy World Cup experience. The same, in terms of his mental strength, could be said of goakeeper Senne Lammens.

Marcus Rashford has returned to the club with a sense of purpose.

After a European based pre-season that should have seen them hit the ground running, Michael Carrick's side have dropped five points from their first three Premier League games.

They have conceded twice in all three. Their opponents are two promoted teams and an Everton outfit whose fans are distraught following a botched deadline day.

Now United must prepare for their Champions League return, against another banana skin-type opponent in Azerbaijan's Sabah FK. After that it is Manchester City .

It is the kind of week they craved 12 months ago. But already, the pressure is on.

"It's not that bad, you know," was Carrick's assessment of his side's start to the season.

"We were that close to coming away with three points today. That's football. There were little moments we can deal with a bit better, but we'll be fine."

Carrick got support in his assessment from his old friend Wayne Rooney, who analysed the Everton game for BBC Sport.

"I thought it was good away performance," he said.

"Obviously, I'd be disappointed with the result, but I thought there was a lot more control in the performance.

"The midfield three were really good. They were two great strikes from Everton which got two goals, but I think there was encouragement from United's point of view. They'll be very frustrated they haven't won the game, given the performance."

"All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that. We're disappointed, bitterly disappointed.

"We can't ignore the fact we have taken a point, but it feels that we should have had a lot more."

If he had wanted, Carrick could have played the 'one of those things' cards about the result at the Hill Dickinson stadium.

After all, the visitors controlled long periods, led twice.

The first equaliser was a brutal strike from Tyrique George. The second a blistering last-gasp effort from Ainsley Maitland-Niles introduced for his debut as a substitute.

It was the first time an Everton player had scored from outside the penalty area on their Premier League debut.

No-one was entirely at fault for either. Lammens might have done better at his near post for the first but George's shot was going at some pace.

But Carrick accepts the optics are not great. He also knows the basic reality if a side concedes twice every time they play, they will not win many Premier League games.

"It's two really good strikes from distance from their point of view. Sometimes they fly in the top corner, more often than not they probably don't.

"But we obviously can't ignore it. We need to concede fewer goals to give us a better chance of winning games. There's things we need to get better at as a team."

Questions have been raised about United's lack of recruitment during the latter days of the transfer window, with no striker signed to support Sesko.

It was interesting to note Joshua Zirkzee remained on the bench for a game he could have played in for Everton had United not ruled out the prospect of the Dutch forward joining on loan because they were unable to secure a replacement.

United also opted not to bring in Rayan Ait-Nouri from Manchester City because they did not want to sign a left-back permanently to put pressure on Luke Shaw.

Shaw was one of the visitors' better performers against Everton . The England defender got forward with regularity and it was encouraging to see him provide the cross for Sesko's late header.

"Defensively he was leading and he was good going forward as well. He looked more of a threat today in his connection with Marcus [Rashford]."

To that end, Carrick will hope the "something" Rashford felt that led to his second-half exit is not serious.

"Marcus and Luke were particularly dangerous down that side," said Carrick.

"They've played together for quite some time now and have an understanding. We're trying to build partnerships and combinations throughout the team."

Shaw has been ever-present in United's Premier League starting line-up since the start of last season.

Now though, Carrick must navigate through a tricky spell of four games in 11 days.

It is the busiest period he has had as United boss. Last term, neither of his two midweek games were followed by weekend matches.

How involved will Shaw be? If he does not play, who starts? Does Zirkzee really have a meaningful role?

Sesko, presumably, has put himself in line to start against Sabah? Or does Carrick prioritise the derby instead.

These are the unanswered questions that would always come in a campaign that could feature 60 games.

The tricky bit is navigating through, while delivering positive results.

"Not that bad" is a fair assessment after three games. But Carrick knows expectations around Manchester United are huge. We are nowhere near reaching it just yet, but there will come a point where "not that bad" will not be good enough.

articles.title: Arteta le enseña a Xabi Alonso quién manda en la Premier
articles.standfirst: El Arsenal, colíder con pleno de puntos, acaba con el invicto del Chelsea
articles.summary: El Arsenal, colíder con pleno de puntos, acaba con el invicto del Chelsea
articles.body: Hasta en siete ocasiones se enfrentaron Mikel Arteta y Xabi Alonso, que comenzaron su carrera juntos en el Antiguoko, como futbolistas. El balance favorece a Xabi: tres victorias, dos empates y dos derrotas. "La historia que nos une y enfrentarnos el uno al otro a este nivel es algo increíble", admitía Arteta antes de cruzarse, por primera vez, en los banquillos. Un primer enfrentamiento que ha caído del lado de Arteta. El Arsenal ha puesto fin al invicto del Chelsea (2-1) para situarse colíder de la Premier junto al Manchester City. Ambos, con nueve puntos. Los 'blues' se quedan cuartos con seis. El derbi, sin embargo, no pudo empezar mejor para los de Xabi Alonso. A los 76 segundos ya ganaban 0-1. Morgan Rogers, que dio 'calabazas' al Arsenal este verano, empaló desde la frontal un balón peinado por Jorrel Hato para batir, por primera vez, a David Raya en lo que va de Premier. Otra vez el Chelsea volvía a golpear primero. Marcó en el minuto 1 en la victoria ante el Fulham (2-3), en el 4' en el triunfo frente al Brighton (4-3) y en el 2' en el Emirates. En esta ocasión, el desenlace fue distinto. Los aficionados 'blues' aprovechaban para presumir de ser el único equipo de Londres que ha ganado la Champions... pero el Arsenal no tardó en recordarles quién es el vigente campeón de la Premier. El gol anulado a Riccardo Calafiori en el 11' sirvió de primer aviso. Se lució 'El Dibu' en un remate a quemarropa de Saka en el 18' y respondió a Raya con un paradón, en dos tiempos, para desviar un 'obús' de Reece James desde 30 metros. Buscaba contragolpear el Chelsea. El Arsenal, en cambio, amasaba balón por derecha. Así llegó el 1-1 en el 25'. Arrancó Kai Havertz pegado a banda, tiró la diagonal hacia el medio y batió al 'Dibu' -pudo hacer más- con un tiro al palo corto con la zurda. El alemán es una pesadilla para sus ex: es al equipo que más goles (3) le ha marcado en Premier desde que abandonó Stamford Bridge. El Chelsea no se fue ganando al descanso por cuestión de centímetros. Pedro Neto recibió un gran envío en largo de Joao Pedro, encaró a Gabriel Magalhaes y vio cómo su disparo se estrellaba con el poste en el añadido de la primera mitad. El Arsenal, en cambio, no perdonó nada más salir del descanso. Fue un calco del 1-1, sólo que esta vez por la izquierda. Christos Tzolis cortó hacia el medio y filtró un pase que dejó pasar Havertz, magistral, para que Martin Odegaard fusilara al Chelsea en el 50'. Se volvía a repetir el guión del primer tiempo, con Raya negándole el gol a Palmer en el 63' y 'El Dibu' luciéndose a disparo de Bukayo Saka en el 69'. El Chelsea movió el banquillo dando entrada a Pep Chavarría, Malo Gusto y Estevao... pero el marcador ya no se movió. Y no se puede decir que no lo intentaran. Raya se lució con una parada marca de la casa para enviar a córner un tiro a la escuadra de Estevao en el 89'. Xabi Alonso ya sabe que el que manda en Londres y en la Premier, ahora mismo, es Arteta.

articles.title: Erling Haaland scripts history, breaks Ronaldo and Mbappe’s scoring record with 300 club goals
articles.summary: Football News: Erling Haaland reaches the milestone of 300 career club goals as Manchester City triumphs over Coventry City, breaking records and closing in on Sergio Aguero. Discover the details of this historic achievement and what it means for the star striker's future at City.
articles.body: Erling Haaland has done what he has become so accustomed to doing: score another goal and make history along the way.The Norway striker reached 300 club career goals as Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the Premier League season with a 1-0 victory over newly promoted Coventry City at the Etihad Stadium.It was another milestone in a career that has moved at extraordinary speed, although one familiar name still sits ahead of him.Haaland reaches 300 goals in another landmark nightHaaland needed just 368 appearances across spells with Molde, Red Bull Salzburg, Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City to reach 300 club goals.That puts him behind only Lionel Messi, who reached the same mark in 365 appearances, while Haaland got there faster than both Kylian Mbappé, who needed 398 games, and Cristiano Ronaldo, who took 499.Messi's record has stood since 2013, when he scored his 300th and 301st goals for Barcelona against Granada.There is an important distinction, though. Messi reached the milestone entirely with Barcelona, whereas Haaland's 300 goals have been spread across four clubs.Haaland's latest came in the 26th minute against Coventry, when he rose to meet a precise cross from Antoine Semenyo and powered a header into the net.Semenyo had received an excellent pass from Enzo Fernández before delivering from the right, with Haaland providing the decisive finish.The goal was enough to give new Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca a perfect start to life in the post-Pep Guardiola era, despite the home side being unable to add to their lead.Haaland, however, felt City should have made the result considerably more comfortable.“I should have scored more goals to finish the game off but I didn't so I made it difficult for the team and managed to keep Coventry in the game until the end,” he told ESPN's Renato Senise. “In the Premier League if you don't execute it will be difficult.”It was Haaland's third goal in two games, another reminder that while City have undergone an enormous rebuild, their most reliable source of goals remains exactly where it was before.The club have spent more than £450 million ($609 million) revamping the squad under Maresca, with deadline-day arrivals including Fernández and Iliman Ndiaye. Both started against Coventry, alongside another major summer signing, Elliot Anderson.Yet Haaland remains City's prize asset.Haaland now has Sergio Aguero's record in his sightsThe 26-year-old has already established himself among Manchester City's greatest goalscorers.Haaland has scored 165 goals in 202 appearances for the club, leaving him second on City's all-time scoring list behind Sergio Aguero, who finished his decade at the Etihad with 260 goals in 390 games.At his current scoring rate, Haaland is on course to overtake Aguero within the next few seasons and become City's outright leading goalscorer.He has already taken one major scoring record away from the Argentine.Haaland became City's all-time leading scorer in the Champions League after reaching 49 goals in the competition, moving two clear of Aguero's tally.For now, though, Messi retains the more eye-catching benchmark: the fastest player to reach 300 club goals in the modern era.Maresca will hardly complain about having Haaland chasing that record while continuing to deliver points for City.“It's an important win, different from the first two,” Maresca said. “I'm very happy. I know the players day-by-day, we know each other. It means we will get better and better.”City are now three points clear of defending champions Arsenal, who face Chelsea on Sunday.The squad around Haaland may look very different from the one Guardiola left behind, but the Norwegian's role has not changed.Give him the chance, and he will keep rewriting the numbers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Odegaard and Saka star - player ratings for Arsenal v Chelsea
articles.summary: How Arsenal and Chelsea's players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Captain Martin Odegaard scored the winner as Arsenal secured an impressive 2-1 home victory over Chelsea .

Club-record £117m signing Morgan Rogers put Chelsea ahead after just two minutes, but Kai Havertz equalised against his former club before Odegaard struck early in the second half to seal the win.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

David Raya : The Arsenal goalkeeper was beaten by the quality of Rogers' finish but dealt comfortably with the other efforts he faced and produced one stunning save late on from Estevao. 6

Ben White : A tidy display in possession, although he made little impact at either end of the pitch. 6

Gabriel Magalhaes : Outshone by Konsa at times but still produced an effective performance. 7

Ezri Konsa : On his first Arsenal start, he won more duels than any other defender and was joint-top for possession won in the first half. 7

Riccardo Calafiori : His underlapping runs were typically adventurous and the Italy defender played a key role in creating problems from set-pieces. 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly : Fired a poor effort wide from the edge of the area late in the first half and was caught in possession in a dangerous area, but competed well in midfield. 6

Declan Rice : Played his part in a fiercely contested midfield battle and contributed well both in and out of possession. 6

Martin Odegaard : Put Arsenal ahead early in the second half with a composed finish. Also impressed with the quality of his delivery, both in open play and from set-pieces. 8

Bukayo Saka : A constant threat from set-pieces and regularly won free-kicks in dangerous positions. His impressive second-half effort was saved. 8

Kai Havertz : Passed up a shooting opportunity in the 23rd minute but made no mistake with his next chance, cutting inside to score two minutes later. Also played a part in Odegaard's goal and proved a threat at set-pieces. 7

Christos Tzolis : Delivered well from the left and provided Arsenal 's main outlet whenever they broke from periods of Chelsea possession. 7

Martin Zubimendi (on 67, Myles-Skelly): A complete substitute performance involving dangerous shots, impressive passing and breaking up the play. 7

Piero Hincapie (on 67, Calafiori): Kept it simple with Arsenal ahead. 6

Mikel Merino (on 77, Odegaard): A tidy addition late on in midfield. 6

Viktor Gyokores (on 78, Havertz): Not much opportunity to make an impact as Arsenal held onto their lead. 5

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, Guimaraes, Dowman

Emiliano Martinez : There was concern when the Argentina goalkeeper was accidentally kicked in the head by Gabriel early on, but he was beaten too easily at his near post for Havertz's equaliser. He later made a high-quality save from Saka in the second half. 5

Josh Acheampong : Often dragged into uncomfortable areas by Tzolis from a tactical perspective, but handled his individual defensive duties well. 6

Maxence Lacroix : Miscontrolled a ball early on and allowed Havertz's shot to pass through his legs but also impressed at other times. 6

Wesley Fofana : Unconvincing defensively against Saka, Odegaard and, ultimately, Havertz for the equaliser, but the most composed of Chelsea 's defenders in possession. 6

Pedro Neto : Tasked with marking Calafiori while also providing an attacking threat. Hit the post just before half-time with a brilliant curling effort. 7

Reece James : Saw a well-struck long-range effort saved after 22 minutes and was arguably Chelsea 's best passer. 7

Romeo Lavia : Produced a superb defensive header to clear the danger in the 32nd minute and competed aggressively throughout. 6

Jorrel Hato : His determination helped create Rogers' volley and he matched that effort defensively, although he struggled to contain Saka at times. 6

Cole Palmer : Had one effort on target in the first half and was booked for a professional foul. Also had a second-half shot saved. Arsenal largely kept him quiet. 5

Morgan Rogers : Opened the scoring with a first-time volley after just two minutes. Later curled an effort narrowly wide in the 31st minute and was Chelsea 's most dangerous attacking player. 7

Joao Pedro : Unconvincing defensively at set-pieces and had few opportunities in front of goal, including an ambitious effort from distance. Still made a significant contribution through his work-rate, physical presence and ability to bring team-mates into play as the number nine. 6

Malo Gusto (on 60, Lavia): Poor effort moments after coming on, albeit playing out of position in central midfield. 5

Pep Chavarria (on 60, Hato): Struggled to track his runners on a few occasions. 6

Estevao Willian (on 80, Neto): The Brazilian's sensational curling effort almost levelled but was saved by Raya.

Subs not used: Penders, Colwill, Barco, Quenda, Gittens

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Real Madrid coaches believe key player should do more in midfield this season
articles.summary: After three successive wins to start the season, a 1-0 loss to Real Betis came as a reality check for Real Madrid, who are still some way off matching the qu...
articles.body:
After three successive wins to start the season, a 1-0 loss to Real Betis came as a reality check for Real Madrid, who are still some way off matching the quality and consistency of Barcelona.

In light of the defeat, the Real Madrid coaching staff is analysing the best way to get the most out of the current setup.

Valverde must improve in coming matches. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

According to Defensa Central , one of the key conclusions drawn from the Betis defeat is that Real Madrid need greater involvement from Federico Valverde with the ball.

The Uruguayan has been deployed as the pivot, largely due to the absence of the injured Aurelien Tchouameni, but he is yet to make the step up in quality the team requires from that role.

While his effort and commitment are never in doubt, Mourinho and his staff, led by Sami Khedira, feel Valverde spends too much time positioned behind the opposition's midfield line.

As a result, he fails to offer passing lanes to his teammates when they are under pressure, forcing them into hurried, aimless clearances rather than playing out cleanly from the back.

That concern has already been communicated to Valverde, who is still adapting to a position he has never truly played, making the challenge all the more difficult for him.

Mourinho must find answers soon. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

However, the problem is not Valverde's alone, with the coaching staff identifying a wider issue in the team's structure.

Khedira has reportedly noted a certain passivity from the attackers in the videos of the match, particularly Vinicius Jr and Kylian Mbappe, when it comes to offering themselves as the ball transitions from midfield into attacking areas.

That lack of movement compounds the difficulties for the deeper midfielders.

Mourinho, for his part, remains unfazed by the departure of Rodri to Barcelona, insisting his squad has the tools to cope.

"I'm not missing Rodri. We have solutions, we have quality," the Portuguese said, before adding that he backs his ability to improve players.

With a Champions League opener against Inter Milan on the horizon , Mourinho and his staff will be keen to iron out these issues quickly.

articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard secure comeback win for champions in pulsating London derby
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Arsenal beat Chelsea 2-1 in a pulsating London derby; Morgan Rogers put Chelsea ahead after 77 seconds against the club that tried to sign him; Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard responded for the Gunners; Arsenal stay perfect at top with Man City
articles.body:
Both London rivals produced a Sunday afternoon treat which rubberstamped Arsenal's credentials as the team to beat - and Chelsea's as worthy challengers for the top honours.

A pulsating game started right from the off as Morgan Rogers - sought after by Arsenal this summer - crashed new club Chelsea ahead after just 77 seconds. That poked the bear of the champions - who produced a response.

Latest news and rumours: Chelsea | Arsenal

After Riccardo Calafiori saw a goal disallowed for offside, former Blue Kai Havertz got his fourth goal against his old club for Arsenal with a strike from the edge of the box.

But despite a dominant Arsenal display, Chelsea still went inches away from a second as Rogers curled wide and Pedro Neto hit the post.

Arsenal turned the tide after the break as Martin Odegaard scored his second goal of the season via a slick team move - which was a carbon copy of the attack that saw him score in the Community Shield against Man City.

And despite some half chances for Chelsea, it was Arsenal who looked more likely to add to their tally - as Emiliano Martinez smartly kept out Bukayo Saka and Ezri Konsa in quick succession. That was until Estevao produced an 89th-minute curler - which needed tipping over by David Raya.

The result means Arsenal stay perfect - level with Manchester City after three games. But Chelsea have shown they will not be far behind...

77 seconds: GOAL! Rogers fires Chelsea in front from the edge of the box after a free-kick is cleared into his path.

5: SCRAMBLE! Arsenal try to hit back through Odegaard's low free-kick but Calafiori and Gabriel fail to convert from close range amid a goalmouth scramble.

12: GOAL DISALLOWED! Another low free-kick from Declan Rice leads to another scramble and this time Calafiori taps home - but Konsa is flagged in an offside position in the build-up.

18: BIG SAVE! Arsenal's onslaught continues as Saka is denied by Martinez down the right wing with a solid stop.

25: GOAL! Havertz beats Martinez at the near post with a drive from the edge of the box.

31: CLOSE! Rogers nearly has a second but his curling effort from inside the box bends just wide.

45+3: OFF THE POST! Neto strikes the woodwork after another Chelsea breakaway.

50: GOAL! Odegaard latches onto Christos Tzolis' pass - via Havertz's smart dummy - to crash in Arsenal's second.

61: OVER! Chelsea substitute Malo Gusto curls over a good chance on the edge of the box after being set up by Neto.

69: WHAT A SAVE! Martinez denies Saka from putting Arsenal in control with a fingertip stop.

72: ANOTHER SAVE! Martinez stops Konsa's header from Saka's corner on the goalline.

89: WHAT A SAVE! Estevao's late curler denied by stunning Raya palm over the crossbar.

Why other teams will be worried about Arsenal

"I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that William Saliba, - who is genuinely world-class and arguably probably the best centre-back in world football - has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it doesn't look like anyone can score against them.

"There is a massive gulf between both teams - their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today.

"We don't normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They're so strong defensively they don't need to get involved in those games.

"They still didn't look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box."

articles.title: WSL talking points: London City, Arsenal and Man City make winning starts on opening weekend, but Chelsea and Man Utd stutter
articles.summary: All the key talking points from the opening weekend of the WSL season; London City Lionesses galactico era kicks off with a win, but more consistency is needed to be a threat; Chelsea and Man Utd off the pace and fall behind rivals Arsenal and Man City
articles.body:
Manchester City took some time to find their usual standards but after the nerves were settled by Mary Fowler's opener, they quickly reminded everyone why they are champions and why they will be well amongst the title race once more.

Fowler's chance was gifted to them by Birmingham but the precision made the difference. Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw rising highest on two occasions to glance home her double has already set the tone for another goal-laden campaign.

There is more to come from City, as Jade Rose's error in the 90th minute highlighted, but the fact they can win so emphatically while not at their best will strike fear in the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea as we settle in for another enthralling WSL season.

Arsenal need more but reinforcements helping already

Like Manchester City, Arsenal were short on their usual standards in front of goal. Alessia Russo and Stina Blackstenius both squandered chances from close range but it looks as if Renee Slegers has a few new names to rely on now.

It has been a summer of change at the club but new signings Lisa Baum and Georgia Stanway stood out and were duly needed in the narrow win against Brighton.

Baum introduced herself in perfect fashion with her emphatic opener after dancing into the box. She then stung the hands of Chiamaka Nnadozie with a similar effort after cutting in from the left during the second half.

Despite her age, Baum displays confidence and talent beyond her years and looks ready-made for the WSL.

Meanwhile, Stanway settled into her role as if she had never left the top flight of English football.

The Lionesses midfielder was the first midfielder in history to record 100+ passes on their league debut for a club and dictated play from the middle of the pitch throughout.

There is more to come from Arsenal and they will need their star players to get up to speed quickly if they are to keep pace with City - but for now, it looks like the reinforcements they have added are ready to contribute.

A lot of eyes would’ve been on Chelsea to start the season strongly. For the first time since 2019, they started a WSL campaign not as defending champions. A statement of intent was needed.

The same can also be said of Manchester United. After missing out on the Champions League, the pressure to return was already on. Then came Marc Skinner’s departure and Eva Olid’s appointment. Starting the new era with a win was of utmost importance.

Neither managed to be convincing. For the latter, perhaps some grace can be given. The transition in coaches, the hype surrounding the new-look London City and a transfer window in which Olid admitted the focus had shifted to January meant there was an uphill struggle. The way they were dominated, though, will give the former Hearts boss much to ponder.

As for the Blues, Lauren James’ opener was a positive. Yet, despite 34 total attempts and an xG of 3.6, the majority of Stamford Bridge was left wanting more.

Buurman’s late own goal will be a tough pill to swallow, but is as a result of Sonia Bompastor’s side not putting the game to bed earlier. With Arsenal and Man City getting off the mark with wins, this false start is the last thing the team once at the pinnacle of English women’s football needed. After one game, they are already part of the chasing pack.

Galactico era off and running but London City need consitency

A debut for Alexia Putellas, as well as debuts for Rosa Kafaji, Mapi Leon and Janni Thomsen, grabbed the headlines in the build-up to the game but London City Lionesses didn't need their stars to shine to beat Manchester United.

An own goal from Julia Zigiotti and a moment of magic from Danielle van de Donk were enough to secure the victory. It was comfortable from minute one for the hosts at a sold-out Hayes Lane but consistency will now be at the forefront of everyone's thinking as they push ahead with the season.

It was something that was lacking from their debut campaign in the WSL but now, fuelled by the talent they have recruited in a stunning summer transfer window, it will now be key.

Michele Kang was asked about how the club will measure success this season before kick-off. She was hesitant to say trophies will be needed.

The club have the talent at their disposal to compete for titles this season but consistency is one issue you cannot address in the window. It has to be earned, week in and week out, as a team.

Coming into a new league is always a challenge. Therefore, not getting off to a winning start is not the end of the world. However, the nature of performances is what matters.

In that respect, Birmingham may come away with their heads held high. Being picked to face the champions away from home on the opening day is arguably the worst start imaginable. But for 45 minutes they held their own until finally City’s quality shone through.

Amy Merricks couldn’t have asked for much more. There will be a sense inside the Blues dressing room that if they can replicate that effort and frustrate teams to that extent every game, they will find a way to survive.

For Charlton, though, there will be a sense of disappointment. While Liverpool aren’t a side to be sniffed at, it did take them 13 games last season to get a win. At home, the Addicks may have had higher hopes. But they just weren’t at the races. Vivien Endemann’s quality was a small taste of what they can expect moving forward. If their response continues to be the same, they will surely be in trouble come the end of the season.

Then there’s Crystal Palace, who bounced back in style. A debut goal for Lexi Lloyd-Smith, a clean sheet and a job well done against Everton. After a year away from the top flight, that was exactly what the doctor ordered. And, to cap it off, it was a good performance. They were close to a second and despite having less of the ball were competitive with Everton, who only truly pushed right at the very end.
